notes:
Direct Driver over the card entry symbol magscope.python_microscope:PythonMicroscopeFocusMotor (confirmed at magscope/python_microscope.py:142) for the focus axis of a python-microscope stage. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's python-object/PythonObjectDriver helper was not used; the adapter has a small motion interface (move_absolute, get_current_z, get_is_moving, get_position_limits) and the package needs decorated reads, an operator_required target and a catalogue focus action, so this is a direct Driver like the exemplar. Z is published in um and the native adapter receives nm; the operator's position_scale must make the adapter report MagScope Z in nm (docs/source/connect_hardware.rst:75). The Z target is Limit.operator_required because no text file of the clone states a stage travel range: the adapter reads the connected axis' limits at run time (magscope/python_microscope.py:214-220); site-limits.example.json only shows an example overlay and its -100..100 um range is not a statement about any stage. NOT COVERED: the upstream camera frames and CameraManager/DummyCamera classes, the acquisition video buffer, and ZLUTGenerationManager; this package binds the focus-axis adapter only. The cap.imaging.focus.v1 input method is narrowed to manual and none because the adapter has no autofocus search, so the upstream autofocus method is not offered. The @estop commands the axis to its reported current position (move_absolute); the adapter has no dedicated stop call, and this R1 package does not claim an independent hardware stop. The hardware path (native.py) was never run and no hardware run is claimed; the package is model-authored and unreviewed. No x-cap ids were used, so there are no catalogue_requests.
